site_settings.value: Welcome to the official digital portal of the Department of Statistics, Nnamdi Azikiwe University. In an era increasingly governed by empirical data, statistical sciences stand at the epicenter of evidence-based innovation, decision-making, and technological advancement. Our department is firmly committed to delivering world-class statistical education that equips students with robust mathematical foundations, modern programming proficiencies, and practical analytical prowess. Whether you are navigating course requirements, accessing past exam papers, preparing for SIWES, or exploring research domains, this platform is engineered to support your academic journey. We charge every student to embrace the ethos of our discipline: precision, critical inquiry, and facts from figures.

The Department of Statistics at Nnamdi Azikiwe University (UNIZIK), Awka, is situated within the Faculty of Physical Sciences. Since its inception, the department has grown into a premier national center for statistical education, applied demographic research, biometric modeling, and econometrics. Our programs are designed to cultivate intellectual rigor, computational agility, and ethical integrity. Today, data is the central currency of human decision-making: from biomedical clinical trials to algorithmic trading, artificial intelligence, national census tracking, and climate informatics. Our graduates lead statistical divisions in the civil service, global technology companies, and multilateral development banks.

To be a globally recognized center of statistical excellence, producing top-tier statisticians and data scientists capable of pioneering innovations in quantitative methodology and transforming socioeconomic development.

To provide robust undergraduate and postgraduate education steeped in mathematical foundations and computational technology, fostering high-impact empirical research that provides actionable solutions to industry and governance.

The philosophy of the Department of Statistics is rooted in the conviction that empirical reality is best understood and optimized through rigorous probabilistic reasoning, mathematical formulation, and computational data exploration. We nurture students to transition from descriptive observers into predictive modelers and strategic decision architects.

The department features a 60-seat Computational Statistics & Data Science Laboratory equipped with modern workstations, statistical suites (R, Python, SPSS, Stata, SAS), a high-speed fiber internet backbone, departmental library holding over 1,500 specialized statistical reference volumes, and seminar presentation auditoriums.
Statistics Admintrative Office, Ground floor, New Physical Sciences Building, science village, Unizik, Awka

courses.title: Communication in English
courses.description: Effective communication in English, grammatical structure, reading comprehension, study skills, phonetics, sentence construction, note-taking, and academic essay composition.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Study skills, active listening and note-taking techniques.
Unit 2: Grammatical structures, sentence types, clauses, and concord.
Unit 3: Phonetics, phonology, and accurate pronunciation.
Unit 4: Reading comprehension and vocabulary expansion.
Unit 5: Academic paragraph and formal essay development.

courses.title: Humanities
courses.description: Introduction to humanities, cultural heritage, social institutions, philosophy, arts, literature, ethics, and human values in contemporary African society.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: The concept, nature, and branches of humanities.
Unit 2: African traditional civilization and colonial impact.
Unit 3: Philosophy, moral ethics, and social justice.
Unit 4: Arts, music, and literary expressions in Nigeria.
Unit 5: Contemporary globalization, cultural preservation, and national identity.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science
courses.description: Foundations of computer systems, computer hardware architecture, system software, binary and hexadecimal arithmetic, problem-solving algorithms, flowcharts, and operating system concepts.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: History and generational evolution of computers.
Unit 2: Hardware architecture: CPU, memory, I/O devices, and storage.
Unit 3: Number systems: binary, octal, decimal, and hexadecimal conversions.
Unit 4: Logic gates and Boolean representation.
Unit 5: Algorithm design, pseudocode, flowchart conventions, and intro to programming.

courses.title: Elementary Mathematics I
courses.description: Elementary set theory, subsets, operations on sets, Venn diagrams, real number system, indices, surds, logarithms, quadratic equations, progressions (AP & GP), and mathematical induction.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Set theory: union, intersection, complement, Cartesian products, and Venn diagrams.
Unit 2: Real number axioms, inequalities, and absolute values.
Unit 3: Indices, logarithms, surds, and radical equations.
Unit 4: Theory of quadratic equations, roots, and polynomial factorization.
Unit 5: Arithmetic and Geometric Progressions, binomial theorem, and induction.

courses.title: Descriptive Statistics
courses.description: Definition, nature, and scope of statistics. Methods of data collection, classification, tabulation, frequency distributions, graphical representation, measures of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, and kurtosis.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Nature of statistical inquiry, primary and secondary data collection.
Unit 2: Frequency distribution tables, histograms, ogives, frequency polygons, and pie charts.
Unit 3: Measures of central tendency: Mean (arithmetic, geometric, harmonic), Median, Mode, Quantiles.
Unit 4: Measures of dispersion: Range, Mean Deviation, Variance, Standard Deviation, and Quartile Deviation.
Unit 5: Moments, Pearsonian and Bowley measures of Skewness and Kurtosis.

courses.title: Statistical Inference I
courses.description: Basic concepts of statistical inference, populations, random sampling, introduction to probability concepts, point and interval estimation for large samples, and elementary formulation of hypothesis testing.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Population and sample definitions, parameter vs statistic.
Unit 2: Random sampling techniques and sampling distributions.
Unit 3: Point estimation concepts: unbiasedness, consistency, and standard errors.
Unit 4: Confidence interval construction for population mean and proportion.
Unit 5: Introduction to statistical hypotheses: Null, Alternative, Type I & II errors, and Z-tests.

courses.title: General Physics I
courses.description: Mechanics, thermal physics, properties of matter, dimensional analysis, rectilinear motion, Newton's laws of motion, work, energy, power, rotational dynamics, elasticity, and fluids.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Units, physical dimensions, and dimensional analysis.
Unit 2: Kinematics: vectors, projectiles, velocity, and acceleration.
Unit 3: Newton's laws, friction, momentum conservation, and collisions.
Unit 4: Circular motion, gravitation, work, power, and kinetic/potential energy.
Unit 5: Hydrostatics, Archimedes' principle, surface tension, viscosity, and thermal expansion.

courses.title: General Biology
courses.description: Fundamental biological principles, ultrastructure of living cells, cellular reproduction, mitosis, meiosis, Mendelian genetics, diversity of living organisms, ecology, and energy flow in ecosystems.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Chemical basis of life, macromolecule structure and biological enzymes.
Unit 2: Cellular anatomy: prokaryotic vs eukaryotic organelles and membrane transport.
Unit 3: Cell division: mitosis, meiosis, and gametogenesis.
Unit 4: Classical Mendelian genetics, monohybrid/dihybrid crosses, and sex linkage.
Unit 5: Principles of ecology, ecosystems, trophic pyramids, and environmental conservation.

courses.title: Principles of Economics
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of microeconomics, scarcity, choice, scale of preference, opportunity cost, laws of demand and supply, elasticity, consumer behavior, and price mechanisms.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Basic economic problems: scarcity, choice, opportunity cost, and production possibility curves.
Unit 2: Demand theory: determinants, demand function, and law of demand.
Unit 3: Supply theory: determinants, supply elasticity, and market equilibrium.
Unit 4: Price elasticity, income elasticity, and cross-price elasticity of demand.
Unit 5: Consumer behavior: cardinal utility theory vs ordinal indifference curve approaches.

courses.title: Introduction of Business
courses.description: Nature and scope of business enterprises, environmental factors affecting business, forms of business ownership (sole proprietorship, partnership, companies), management functions, and ethical practices in Nigeria.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Conceptual scope of business, profit motive, and social responsibilities.
Unit 2: Business environments: economic, legal, socio-cultural, and technological factors.
Unit 3: Forms of ownership: sole proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, cooperatives.
Unit 4: Core functional areas: human resources, operations, accounting, and marketing.
Unit 5: Business planning, risk management, and government regulatory frameworks in Nigeria.

courses.title: Nigerian Peoples and Culture
courses.description: Evolution of traditional Nigerian communities, pre-colonial political systems, ethnic nationalities, inter-group interactions, colonial administrative impact, military rule, and modern socio-cultural development.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Pre-colonial political institutions in Northern, Western, and Eastern Nigeria.
Unit 2: Cultural norms, indigenous craftsmanship, religion, and social organization.
Unit 3: Colonial conquest, amalgamation of 1914, and indirect rule systems.
Unit 4: Post-independence political dynamics, nationalism, and federalism.
Unit 5: Ethnic harmony, national integration, and civic responsibility in modern Nigeria.

courses.title: Basic Igbo Studies
courses.description: Study of Igbo orthography, grammar, vocabulary, proverbs, idioms, oral narratives, cultural worldview, traditional institutions, and socio-economic systems of the Igbo people.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Igbo alphabet, vowels, consonants, tone marking, and orthographic rules.
Unit 2: Parts of speech, sentence building, and translation exercises.
Unit 3: Traditional Igbo social hierarchy, title-taking (Ozo), age grades, and kingship.
Unit 4: Igbo folklore, riddles, moral values, and idiomatic expressions (Ilu).
Unit 5: Contemporary Igbo language preservation, digital literacy, and cultural heritage.

courses.title: Probability 1
courses.description: Sample spaces, events, axiomatic definition of probability, addition and multiplication rules, conditional probability, independent events, Bayes' theorem, discrete random variables, and probability mass functions.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Random experiments, elementary outcomes, events, and sample spaces.
Unit 2: Axiomatic probability foundations and basic set-theoretic theorems.
Unit 3: Conditional probability, multiplication rule, and partition of sample spaces.
Unit 4: Law of total probability and Bayes' Theorem with diagnostic applications.
Unit 5: Random variables, probability mass functions, and cumulative distribution functions.

courses.title: Statistical computing 1
courses.description: Practical statistical computing using modern tools (Excel spreadsheets, R, and SPSS). Data entry, data cleansing, tabular presentations, descriptive computations, graphical exploratory analysis, and simulation basics.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Spreadsheet fundamentals: worksheet layout, formulas, and data formatting in Excel.
Unit 2: Summary functions, pivot tables, and statistical charting.
Unit 3: Introduction to R environment: data structures (vectors, data frames, factors).
Unit 4: Descriptive metrics calculation, frequency generation, and boxplots in R & SPSS.
Unit 5: Introduction to reproducible reporting and pseudo-random number generation.

courses.title: Elementary Mathematics II
courses.description: Trigonometric functions, radian measures, addition and factor formulas, limit of a function, differentiation from first principles, product/quotient/chain rules, integration techniques, and area under curves.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Circular trigonometric functions, trigonometric identities, and compound angles.
Unit 2: Function limits, continuity, and concept of derivative from first principles.
Unit 3: Differentiation techniques: product rule, quotient rule, and function of a function.
Unit 4: Applications of derivatives: tangents, normals, rates of change, maxima and minima.
Unit 5: Indefinite and definite integrals, integration by substitution, and basic areas.

courses.title: Physics II
courses.description: Electrostatics, Coulomb's law, electric field and potential, capacitors and dielectrics, electric currents, Ohm's law, DC circuits, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, geometrical optics, and wave motion.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Electric charge, Coulomb's law, electric flux, Gauss's law, and potential.
Unit 2: Capacitance, combination of capacitors, and dielectric properties.
Unit 3: Electric current, resistance, electromotive force, and Kirchhoff's circuit rules.
Unit 4: Magnetic force on moving charges, Biot-Savart law, and Faraday's induction.
Unit 5: Reflection, refraction, lenses, mirrors, and wave interference.

courses.title: Intro to actuarial Mathematics I
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of financial mathematics, theory of interest, simple and compound interest rates, nominal and effective rates, discount factors, present values, annuities-certain, and amortization schedules.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Time value of money, accumulation functions, and interest rate definitions.
Unit 2: Simple vs compound interest, effective vs nominal interest rates.
Unit 3: Discount rates, force of interest, and present value calculations.
Unit 4: Annuities-certain: immediate annuities, annuities-due, and perpetuities.
Unit 5: Loan amortization schedules, sinking funds, and capital redemption.

courses.title: Computer Programming II
courses.description: Principles of structured and procedural computer programming using modern high-level languages (C / Python). Data types, expressions, control structures, functions, parameter passing, arrays, and file I/O.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Language syntax, basic data types, variables, and operator precedence.
Unit 2: Selection structures: if-else branches, switch-case statements.
Unit 3: Repetition structures: while, do-while, and for loops.
Unit 4: Functions, variable scope, recursion, and parameter passing mechanisms.
Unit 5: One-dimensional and multi-dimensional arrays, string processing, and file input/output.

courses.title: General Biology II
courses.description: Comparative study of plant and animal physiology, nutrition, gas exchange, circulatory systems, excretion, nervous coordination, hormones, reproduction, development, and environmental adaptation.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Plant nutrition: photosynthesis, mineral absorption, and transport systems.
Unit 2: Animal nutrition: digestive mechanisms and mammalian enzyme actions.
Unit 3: Respiration, gaseous exchange mechanisms, and mammalian blood circulation.
Unit 4: Osmoregulation, excretory systems, and homeostasis.
Unit 5: Nervous and endocrine coordination, sensory organs, and environmental response.

courses.title: Principles of Economics II
courses.description: Fundamental macroeconomic theory, national income accounting (GDP, GNP, NNP), circular flow of income, aggregate demand and supply, inflation, unemployment, fiscal policy, monetary policy, and external trade.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Scope of macroeconomics and the circular flow of economic activity.
Unit 2: National income accounting: output, income, and expenditure measurement.
Unit 3: Aggregate consumption, savings function, investment multiplier, and equilibrium.
Unit 4: Money, banking institutions, and the role of the Central Bank of Nigeria.
Unit 5: Inflation types, unemployment causes, fiscal policy, and international balance of payments.

courses.title: Introduction To Business II
courses.description: Organizational structures, operational management, production planning, total quality management, human resource management, labor unions, marketing strategies, and international business perspectives.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Organizational theory: classical, bureaucratic, and human relations models.
Unit 2: Production management: plant location, layout, inventory, and supply chain control.
Unit 3: Marketing mix: product design, pricing strategies, distribution, and promotional channels.
Unit 4: Personnel administration: recruitment, selection, training, and performance evaluation.
Unit 5: Labor relations, collective bargaining, and corporate social responsibility in Nigeria.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship and Innovation 2
courses.description: Developing innovative entrepreneurial ventures, opportunity identification, feasibility analysis, business model canvas, financing startups, patenting, intellectual property, and venture lifecycle.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Entrepreneurial mindsets and innovation-driven opportunity evaluation.
Unit 2: Feasibility studies and the Business Model Canvas (BMC) framework.
Unit 3: Startup capitalization: angel investors, venture capital, and commercial bank loans.
Unit 4: Legal registrations, CAC processes, trademarks, and intellectual property protection.
Unit 5: Enterprise scaling, digital transformation, and risk management strategies.

courses.title: Probability II
courses.description: Discrete and continuous random variables, probability mass and density functions, cumulative distribution functions, mathematical expectation, variance, moments, moment generating functions, and standard probability models.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Univariate discrete distributions: Bernoulli, Binomial, Poisson, Geometric, Negative Binomial, Hypergeometric.
Unit 2: Univariate continuous distributions: Uniform, Normal, Exponential, Gamma, Beta, and Weibull.
Unit 3: Mathematical expectations, higher-order moments, and skewness/kurtosis measures.
Unit 4: Moment Generating Functions (MGF) and characteristic functions properties.
Unit 5: Chebyshev's Inequality, Markov's Inequality, and Law of Large Numbers intro.

courses.title: Statistical Inference II
courses.description: Sampling distributions (Student's t, Chi-Square, Snedecor's F), point estimation principles, properties of estimators (unbiasedness, consistency, efficiency, sufficiency), Method of Moments, Maximum Likelihood Estimation, and interval estimation.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Derivations and properties of Chi-Square, t, and F sampling distributions.
Unit 2: Point estimation: concept of estimator properties (unbiasedness, minimum variance, consistency).
Unit 3: Sufficiency and the Fisher-Neyman Factorization Theorem.
Unit 4: Estimation methods: Method of Moments and Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE).
Unit 5: Exact confidence intervals for one and two population means, variances, and proportions.

courses.title: Statistical Computing II
courses.description: Computational statistical algorithms using R and Python. Implementation of probability distribution calculations, pseudo-random variate generation, Monte Carlo simulations, numerical matrix operations, and regression computation.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Intermediate programming in R: control structures, loops, vectorization, and apply family.
Unit 2: Random variate generation methods: inverse transform, acceptance-rejection, Box-Muller.
Unit 3: Monte Carlo simulation of probabilistic processes and approximation of integrals.
Unit 4: Matrix algebra computations: inversion, decomposition (LU, Cholesky), and eigensystems in R.
Unit 5: Implementing custom estimation algorithms (e.g. Newton-Raphson MLE) programmatically.

courses.title: Computer Programming I
courses.description: Object-oriented programming (OOP) paradigms using modern programming languages. Classes, objects, encapsulation, data abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, and exception handling.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: OOP concepts: comparison between procedural and object-oriented paradigms.
Unit 2: Classes, object instantiation, constructors, destructors, and member access specifiers.
Unit 3: Encapsulation, information hiding, getters, and setters.
Unit 4: Single and multiple inheritance, method overriding, and polymorphism.
Unit 5: Abstract base classes, interfaces, and structured exception handling mechanisms.

courses.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods
courses.description: Real-valued functions of several variables, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient vectors, total differentials, Taylor's series for multiple variables, extreme values, Lagrange multipliers, and multiple integrals.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Functions of two or more variables: domains, level curves, and surfaces.
Unit 2: Partial differentiation, higher order partials, and Clairaut's theorem on mixed partials.
Unit 3: Directional derivatives, gradient vector, tangent planes, and total differentials.
Unit 4: Extrema of multi-variable functions, Hessian matrix, and constrained optimization via Lagrange multipliers.
Unit 5: Double and triple integrals, Fubini's theorem, change of variables, and Jacobians.

courses.title: Linear Algebra I
courses.description: Vector spaces over fields, subspaces, linear span, linear independence, basis, dimension, linear mappings, matrix representations of linear mappings, rank-nullity theorem, systems of linear equations, and determinants.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Vector space axioms over fields, linear combinations, and subspaces.
Unit 2: Linear dependence, linear independence, spanning sets, bases, and finite dimensionality.
Unit 3: Linear transformations: kernel, image, Rank-Nullity Theorem, and isomorphisms.
Unit 4: Matrix representation of linear transformations and change of basis matrices.
Unit 5: Systems of linear equations: Gaussian elimination, echelon forms, rank, and determinants.

courses.title: Micro Economics I
courses.description: Intermediate microeconomic analysis: axiomatic consumer theory, utility maximization, Marshallian and Hicksian demand functions, Slutsky equation, production functions, cost minimization, and perfect competition.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Axioms of consumer preference, budget constraints, and utility functions.
Unit 2: Constrained utility maximization, Marshallian vs Compensated (Hicksian) demand.
Unit 3: Slutsky decomposition into income and substitution effects.
Unit 4: Production functions: Isoquants, Marginal Rate of Technical Substitution (MRTS), and Returns to Scale.
Unit 5: Cost function derivations (short-run vs long-run) and profit maximization in competitive markets.

courses.title: Digital Logic Design
courses.description: Boolean algebra, truth tables, logic gates, minimization of Boolean expressions using Karnaugh maps and Quine-McCluskey, combinational logic circuits (adders, multiplexers, decoders), and sequential circuits.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Binary logic, Boolean postulates, De Morgan's laws, and standard forms (SOP, POS).
Unit 2: Logic gate implementations: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR, XNOR.
Unit 3: Simplification techniques: Karnaugh maps up to 5 variables and prime implicants.
Unit 4: Combinational circuits: half/full adders, subtractors, magnitude comparators, multiplexers, decoders.
Unit 5: Latches, flip-flops (SR, JK, D, T), clocking, counters, and basic register design.

courses.title: Principles of Management
courses.description: Theoretical evolution of administrative thought, classical management, behavioral human relations, systems theory, contingency approach, and managerial functions: planning, organizing, staffing, leading, and controlling.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Nature, purpose, and universal principles of administrative management.
Unit 2: Historical schools: Scientific Management (Taylor), Administrative (Fayol), and Bureaucratic (Weber).
Unit 3: Strategic and operational planning: MBO, SWOT analysis, and decision-making techniques.
Unit 4: Organizational structure: centralization vs decentralization, span of control, and departmentalization.
Unit 5: Leadership styles, motivational frameworks (Maslow, Herzberg), and controlling systems.

courses.title: Philosophy, Logic, and Human Existence
courses.description: Scope and major branches of philosophy (epistemology, metaphysics, ethics, aesthetics), logical reasoning, valid argument deduction, propositional logic, categorical syllogisms, informal fallacies, and existential questions.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: The nature, method, and branches of philosophical inquiry.
Unit 2: Epistemology: sources and justification of human knowledge (empiricism vs rationalism).
Unit 3: Propositional logic, connectives, truth tables, and validity testing.
Unit 4: Categorical syllogisms, Euler diagrams, and formal/informal logical fallacies.
Unit 5: Philosophical foundations of science, human rights, justice, and existential meaning.

courses.title: Statistics for Physical Sciences & Engineering
courses.description: Application of statistical methods to engineering and physical science domains: experimental measurement errors, propagation of errors, curve fitting, regression, hypothesis testing, reliability, and quality control.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Physical measurements, random and systematic errors, and error propagation formulas.
Unit 2: Probability models for engineering phenomena (Weibull, Lognormal, Extreme Value distributions).
Unit 3: Method of least squares, linear and polynomial curve fitting for calibration.
Unit 4: Hypothesis tests for material strength, variance comparisons, and ANOVA in lab trials.
Unit 5: Statistical process control, Shewhart charts, and system reliability analysis.

courses.title: Introduction to Social & Economic Statistics
courses.description: Official statistical systems, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) structure, national accounts, index numbers (Laspeyres, Paasche, Fisher), Consumer Price Index (CPI), inflation metrics, vital statistics, and demographic indicators.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: National official statistical architecture: NBS, statistical coordination, and data governance.
Unit 2: Index numbers: simple, weighted aggregate, price and quantity relatives, tests of consistency.
Unit 3: Consumer Price Index (CPI) methodology, inflation computation, and purchasing power parity.
Unit 4: Vital statistics: crude and age-specific birth/death rates, infant mortality, and fertility indices.
Unit 5: Population census procedures, socio-economic surveys, and poverty headcount metrics.

courses.title: Probability and Probability Distribution
courses.description: Bivariate probability distributions, joint probability mass and density functions, marginal and conditional distributions, stochastic independence, covariance, correlation coefficient, conditional expectation, and bivariate normal distribution.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Joint probability distributions of discrete and continuous random variables.
Unit 2: Marginal distributions and conditional probability distributions.
Unit 3: Stochastic independence of random variables and conditional expectation.
Unit 4: Covariance, Pearson correlation coefficient, and properties of variance of sums.
Unit 5: Bivariate transformation techniques and the Bivariate Normal Distribution derivation.

courses.title: Computer Programming II
courses.description: Fundamental data structures and algorithmic complexity. Memory representation, linked lists (singly, doubly), stacks, queues, binary search trees, sorting algorithms (quicksort, mergesort), and graph traversal.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Abstract Data Types (ADT) and algorithmic Big-O asymptotic notation.
Unit 2: Dynamic memory allocation, pointer manipulation, and singly/doubly linked lists.
Unit 3: Stacks and queues: array/pointer implementations, postfix evaluations, and recursion.
Unit 4: Non-linear structures: binary trees, binary search trees, and tree traversals (in/pre/post).
Unit 5: Searching and sorting algorithms: insertion, selection, quicksort, mergesort, and hash tables.

courses.title: Elementary Differential Equation II
courses.description: Second-order linear ordinary differential equations with constant coefficients, undetermined coefficients, variation of parameters, Cauchy-Euler equations, series solutions, Frobenius method, and Laplace transforms.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Second order homogeneous linear ODEs: auxiliary equation and complementary functions.
Unit 2: Non-homogeneous linear ODEs: Method of Undetermined Coefficients and Variation of Parameters.
Unit 3: Cauchy-Euler differential equations and systems of first-order linear ODEs.
Unit 4: Power series solutions around ordinary and regular singular points (Frobenius method).
Unit 5: Laplace transformation, inverse transforms, convolution theorem, and initial value problems.

courses.title: Industrial Training
courses.description: Supervised vacation practical industrial attachment. Exposure to industrial work settings, practical data entry, database logging, statistical summary reporting, and documentation in government, corporate, or research institutions.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Industrial placement orientation, workplace ethics, and safety protocols.
Unit 2: Practical data acquisition, logging, and database auditing workflows.
Unit 3: Applied spreadsheet analysis and weekly statistical logbook maintenance.
Unit 4: Collaborative departmental data presentation and preliminary statistical reporting.
Unit 5: Comprehensive industrial training logbook review and oral departmental evaluation.

courses.title: Linear Algebra II
courses.description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, characteristic polynomials, minimal polynomials, Cayley-Hamilton theorem, matrix diagonalization, inner product spaces, Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process, and quadratic forms.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Characteristic values and characteristic vectors of linear operators.
Unit 2: Characteristic polynomial, algebraic/geometric multiplicity, and Cayley-Hamilton theorem.
Unit 3: Diagonalizability criteria and Jordan Canonical Forms introduction.
Unit 4: Real and complex inner product spaces, Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and orthogonality.
Unit 5: Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization procedure, orthogonal projections, and symmetric matrices.

courses.title: Introduction to Actuarial Mathematics
courses.description: Survival models, force of mortality, life tables, life assurance contracts (whole life, term, endowment), life annuities, net premium determination, and introduction to policy benefit reserves.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Survival distributions, future lifetime random variables, and force of mortality.
Unit 2: Life table construction: lx, dx, qx, px, and fractional age assumptions.
Unit 3: Life assurances: whole life, term assurance, endowment, and pure endowment present values.
Unit 4: Life annuities: continuous, immediate, and due annuity expectations.
Unit 5: Equivalence principle, net single and level annual premium calculations, and reserves.

courses.title: Micro Economics II
courses.description: Market structures: monopoly pricing, price discrimination, monopolistic competition, oligopoly models (Cournot, Bertrand, Stackelberg), game theory introduction, general equilibrium, and welfare economics.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Pure monopoly equilibrium, deadweight loss, and first/second/third degree price discrimination.
Unit 2: Monopolistic competition: short-run and long-run Chamberlinian equilibrium.
Unit 3: Oligopoly theories: Cournot, Bertrand, and Stackelberg leader-follower duopoly models.
Unit 4: Strategic game theory: normal form games, dominant strategies, and Nash Equilibrium.
Unit 5: General equilibrium: Edgeworth box, Pareto optimality, market failures, and externalities.

courses.title: Probability III
courses.description: Advanced probability spaces, distributions of functions of random variables, Jacobian transformation techniques, order statistics and their distributions, multivariate distributions, characteristic functions, and probability inequalities.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Probability spaces, sigma-algebras, Borel sets, and probability measures.
Unit 2: Jacobians of single and multi-variable transformations of random variables.
Unit 3: Order statistics: joint and marginal distributions of smallest, largest, and median values.
Unit 4: Characteristic functions, inversion formula, and uniqueness theorems.
Unit 5: Modes of convergence (in probability, almost surely, in distribution) and Central Limit Theorem.

courses.title: Statistical Inference III
courses.description: Point estimation theory: Fisher information, Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB), efficiency, complete and sufficient statistics, Rao-Blackwell Theorem, Lehmann-Scheffe Theorem, UMVUE, and asymptotic properties.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Likelihood function, score function, and Fisher Information matrix.
Unit 2: Cramer-Rao Lower Bound regularity conditions and proof for unbiased estimators.
Unit 3: Exponential family of probability distributions and complete sufficient statistics.
Unit 4: Rao-Blackwellization and Lehmann-Scheffe theorem for finding UMVUE estimators.
Unit 5: Asymptotic efficiency and normality of Maximum Likelihood Estimators.

courses.title: Statistical Computing III
courses.description: Advanced statistical computing and modeling in R and Python. Resampling methods (bootstrap, jackknife), EM algorithm, numerical optimization (Nelder-Mead, BFGS), Bayesian MCMC basics, and interactive markdown reporting.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Numerical optimization: Newton-Raphson, Fisher scoring, and gradient descent.
Unit 2: Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm for missing data and mixture models.
Unit 3: Non-parametric bootstrap: standard error, bias estimation, and BCa confidence intervals.
Unit 4: Jackknife resampling and cross-validation techniques for model selection.
Unit 5: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) intro: Metropolis-Hastings and Gibbs sampling.

courses.title: Regression Analysis I
courses.description: Simple and multiple linear regression, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) estimation in matrix notation, Gauss-Markov theorem, coefficient of determination, hypothesis testing on regression coefficients, and ANOVA in regression.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Simple linear regression: assumptions, derivation of OLS estimators, and properties.
Unit 2: Multiple linear regression in matrix notation: Y = Xb + e, normal equations, and (X'X)^-1.
Unit 3: Gauss-Markov theorem and proof that OLS is BLUE (Best Linear Unbiased Estimator).
Unit 4: Tests of significance: t-tests for coefficients, overall F-test, and R-squared/adjusted R-squared.
Unit 5: Confidence intervals and prediction intervals for mean responses and individual forecasts.

courses.title: Analysis of Variance I
courses.description: Linear statistical models, fixed and random effects, one-way classification, Completely Randomized Design (CRD), two-way classification with and without interaction, Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD), and Latin Square Design (LSD).
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Linear models: fixed, random, and mixed effects model definitions.
Unit 2: One-way ANOVA and Completely Randomized Design (CRD) partition of sums of squares.
Unit 3: Post-hoc multiple comparison tests: Fisher's LSD, Tukey's HSD, Duncan's Multiple Range, Scheffe's.
Unit 4: Two-way ANOVA without interaction: RCBD model, relative efficiency, and missing plots.
Unit 5: Latin Square Design: model specification, layout, ANOVA table, and efficiency relative to CRD.

courses.title: Demography
courses.description: Demographic data collection, errors in demographic data, mortality analysis, fertility indices, reproduction rates, complete and abridged life tables, population growth models, population estimation, and demographic transition.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Nature of demography, sources of data, census procedures, and post-enumeration surveys.
Unit 2: Evaluation of age and sex data: Whipple's Index, Myers' Blended Index, and UN Age-Sex Index.
Unit 3: Measures of mortality: crude death rate, age-specific death rates, infant mortality, and standardization.
Unit 4: Measures of fertility: CBR, GFR, ASFR, Total Fertility Rate (TFR), GRR, and NRR.
Unit 5: Life tables: construction of complete/abridged life tables, stationary populations, and projections.

courses.title: Operations Research I
courses.description: Introduction to operations research, mathematical modeling, Linear Programming (LP) formulation, graphical solution method, the Simplex algorithm, artificial variable techniques (Big M, Two-Phase), and duality theory.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: History, methodology, and mathematical formulation of Linear Programming problems.
Unit 2: Graphical solution method for two-variable linear optimization models.
Unit 3: The Simplex algorithm: tableau construction, pivot operations, and optimality criteria.
Unit 4: Artificial variable methods: Big-M method and Two-Phase Simplex technique.
Unit 5: Duality in linear programming: primal-dual relationships, economic interpretation, and dual simplex.

courses.title: Biometry
courses.description: Statistical methods in biological, agricultural, and medical research: bioassays, direct and indirect assays, parallel-line and slope-ratio assays, quantal response assays, probit and logit analysis, LD50 estimation, and clinical trials.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Scope of biometry and characteristics of biological variation.
Unit 2: Principles of biological assay: direct assays and precision estimation.
Unit 3: Quantitative indirect assays: parallel-line assays and slope-ratio assays.
Unit 4: Quantal response assays: dose-response curves, Probit transformation, Logit model, and LD50/ED50.
Unit 5: Clinical trial design: randomization, blinding, ethical considerations, and cross-over designs.

courses.title: Peace and Conflict Resolution
courses.description: Conflict analysis, root causes of ethnic, religious, and political disputes in Africa, conflict mapping, crisis de-escalation, alternative dispute resolution (ADR), negotiation, mediation, arbitration, and peacebuilding.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Conceptual definitions of peace, conflict, violence, and security.
Unit 2: Theories of conflict: structural, biological, economic, and human needs theories.
Unit 3: Conflict dynamics in Nigeria: resource control, ethnicity, religious clashes, and terrorism.
Unit 4: Conflict transformation mechanisms: communication, negotiation, mediation, and arbitration.
Unit 5: Post-conflict peacebuilding, disarmament, demobilization, rehabilitation, and rule of law.

courses.title: Venture Creation
courses.description: Practical enterprise creation, commercialization of scientific ideas, business plan preparation, financial forecasting, product prototyping, digital marketing, corporate regulatory compliance, and managing sustainable ventures.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Ideation, lean startup methodologies, and minimal viable product (MVP) design.
Unit 2: Market research, customer discovery, competitor benchmarking, and value propositions.
Unit 3: Financial planning: cash flow statements, break-even analysis, and balance sheet forecasting.
Unit 4: Operational setup: supply chains, intellectual property filing, and CAC incorporation.
Unit 5: Pitching to investors, venture governance, scaling strategies, and exit avenues.

courses.title: Distribution theory I
courses.description: Advanced distribution theory: Pearson system of distributions, compound distributions, truncated distributions, convolutions of random variables, order statistics distributions, and multivariate probability families.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: The Pearson family of frequency curves: differential equation and classification of types.
Unit 2: Compound and mixture distributions: Poisson-Gamma (Negative Binomial), Binomial-Beta.
Unit 3: Truncated distributions: left, right, and doubly truncated probability models.
Unit 4: Sums and convolutions of independent random variables using transforms.
Unit 5: Sampling distributions derived from normal populations and non-central distributions.

courses.title: Survey methods and sampling theory
courses.description: Principles and practice of sample surveys: survey planning, questionnaire design, sampling and non-sampling errors, Simple Random Sampling (SRS), Stratified Random Sampling, optimum allocation, Systematic Sampling, and Cluster Sampling.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Planning and execution of sample surveys, sampling frame, questionnaire design, and pre-testing.
Unit 2: Simple Random Sampling (SRSWOR & SRSWR): estimation of population mean, total, and variances.
Unit 3: Stratified Random Sampling: proportional allocation, Neyman allocation, and gain in precision.
Unit 4: Systematic sampling: circular and linear systematic selection, and comparison with SRS.
Unit 5: Cluster sampling with equal clusters, two-stage sampling, and non-sampling error reduction.

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control I
courses.description: Statistical quality control philosophy, control charts for variables (X-bar, R, and S charts), control charts for attributes (p, np, c, and u charts), operating characteristic curves, process capability analysis, and acceptance sampling.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Quality concepts, Deming philosophy, chance and assignable causes of process variation.
Unit 2: Shewhart control charts for variables: X-bar and R charts, trial control limits, and interpretation.
Unit 3: Control charts for attributes: fraction nonconforming (p and np charts) and defects (c and u charts).
Unit 4: Process capability indices: Cp, Cpk, and Cpm calculations and interpretations.
Unit 5: Acceptance sampling for attributes: single sampling plans, OC curves, AQL, and LTPD.

courses.title: Statistical Methods In Epidemiology
courses.description: Statistical methods in public health: epidemiological study designs (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional), measures of disease occurrence, measures of association (relative risk, odds ratio), confounding, standardization, and survival curves.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Fundamental principles of epidemiology, disease causation, and observational study designs.
Unit 2: Measures of disease frequency: incidence rate, incidence proportion (risk), and prevalence.
Unit 3: Measures of association: Risk Ratio (RR), Odds Ratio (OR), Attributable Risk, and population AR.
Unit 4: Confounding and interaction (effect modification): Mantel-Haenszel stratified methods.
Unit 5: Standardization of rates (direct and indirect) and introduction to Kaplan-Meier survival curves.

courses.title: Statistical Application of Matrix Algebra
courses.description: Matrix operations in statistical theory: partitioned matrices, determinants, trace properties, generalized inverses (Moore-Penrose), idempotent matrices, quadratic forms, eigenvalues, spectral decomposition, and distributions of quadratic forms.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Review of matrix operations: partitioned matrices, Kronecker products, trace, and rank.
Unit 2: Generalized inverses (g-inverses): definitions, Moore-Penrose inverse, and solving linear systems.
Unit 3: Idempotent matrices, projection operators, and orthogonal projections in linear models.
Unit 4: Quadratic forms: positive definiteness, spectral decomposition, and differentiation with respect to vectors.
Unit 5: Distribution of quadratic forms, Cochran's Theorem, and independence of linear and quadratic forms.

courses.title: Industrial Attachment
courses.description: Supervised Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme (SIWES). Six months of practical professional attachment in industry, financial banks, research institutes, or statistical agencies applying quantitative skills to live data operations.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Industrial placement registration, employer orientation, and industrial safety compliance.
Unit 2: Active operational engagement in statistical data collection, cleaning, and database reporting.
Unit 3: Weekly logbook documentation of technical statistical tasks, programming scripts, and analyses.
Unit 4: Institutional supervisory visits and mid-attachment performance appraisals.
Unit 5: Submission of comprehensive SIWES technical report and oral defense before departmental board.

courses.title: Probability IV
courses.description: Measure-theoretic probability foundations: sigma-fields, measurable spaces, probability measures, Lebesgue-Stieltjes integrals, Radon-Nikodym theorem, conditional expectation given a sigma-field, martingales, and convergence theorems.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Measure theory foundations: algebras, sigma-algebras, Borel fields, and outer measures.
Unit 2: Measurable functions, random variables as measurable mappings, and integration theory.
Unit 3: Monotone Convergence Theorem, Fatou's Lemma, and Lebesgue Dominated Convergence Theorem.
Unit 4: Radon-Nikodym derivative and conditional expectation with respect to sub-sigma-fields.
Unit 5: Martingales: discrete-parameter sub-martingales, super-martingales, and Doob's Optional Stopping Theorem.

courses.title: Statistical Inference IV
courses.description: Advanced hypothesis testing theory: Neyman-Pearson fundamental lemma, Uniformly Most Powerful (UMP) tests, monotone likelihood ratio (MLR) property, unbiased tests (UMPU), Likelihood Ratio Tests (LRT), and sequential probability ratio tests.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: General formulation of statistical hypothesis testing and randomized test functions.
Unit 2: Neyman-Pearson Fundamental Lemma: statement, proof, and construction of Most Powerful tests.
Unit 3: Families with Monotone Likelihood Ratio (MLR) and derivation of one-sided UMP tests.
Unit 4: Two-sided hypotheses, concept of unbiasedness, and Uniformly Most Powerful Unbiased (UMPU) tests.
Unit 5: Likelihood Ratio Test (LRT) construction, asymptotic Chi-Square distribution, and Wald's SPRT.

courses.title: Times Analysis
courses.description: Time Series Analysis: stationary and non-stationary processes, autocovariance and autocorrelation functions (ACF/PACF), Box-Jenkins AR, MA, ARMA, and ARIMA models, unit root testing, spectral analysis, and forecasting.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Time series components, stationarity definitions (strict vs weak), autocovariance, and ACF.
Unit 2: Autoregressive (AR), Moving Average (MA), and mixed ARMA stochastic processes and conditions.
Unit 3: Non-stationary series: difference-stationarity, ARIMA models, and Box-Jenkins three-stage methodology.
Unit 4: Unit root tests: Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) and Phillips-Perron tests for stationarity.
Unit 5: Forecasting techniques, prediction error variance, and introduction to ARCH/GARCH volatility models.

courses.title: Regression Analysis II
courses.description: Advanced regression methodology: multicollinearity diagnostics, ridge regression, LASSO, model selection criteria (AIC, BIC, Mallows' Cp), residual diagnostics, non-linear regression, and Generalized Linear Models (GLMs).
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Multicollinearity: detection (VIF, Condition Number) and remedial ridge/lasso shrinkage methods.
Unit 2: Regression model diagnostics: studentized residuals, leverage values, Cook's distance, and outliers.
Unit 3: Model selection strategies: stepwise regression, best subsets, AIC, BIC, and cross-validation.
Unit 4: Polynomial and non-linear regression estimation via Gauss-Newton iterative algorithms.
Unit 5: Generalized Linear Models (GLMs): link functions, logistic regression, and Poisson regression.

courses.title: Design And Analysis of Experiment
courses.description: Advanced experimental design: factorial experiment structures (2^k and 3^k series), complete and partial confounding, fractional factorial replication, split-plot designs, nested designs, and Response Surface Methodology (RSM).
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Factorial designs: main effects, two-factor and three-factor interactions in 2^k factorials.
Unit 2: Confounding in 2^k factorials: complete confounding, partial confounding, and defining contrasts.
Unit 3: Fractional factorial designs: 2^(k-p) designs, resolution III, IV, and V, and alias structures.
Unit 4: Split-plot and split-block experimental layouts, models, and ANOVA partitioning.
Unit 5: Response Surface Methodology: central composite designs, steepest ascent, and stationary points.

courses.title: Multivariate Analysis I
courses.description: Multivariate normal distributions, properties of random vectors and covariance matrices, Hotelling's T-squared distribution, testing multivariate hypotheses on mean vectors, Multivariate Analysis of Variance (MANOVA), and Principal Component Analysis.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Multivariate random vectors: mean vector, dispersion matrix, and multivariate normal density.
Unit 2: Sampling distributions of sample mean vector and Wishart distribution of sample covariance matrix.
Unit 3: Hotelling's T-squared statistic: one-sample and two-sample tests for mean vectors.
Unit 4: One-way and two-way MANOVA: Wilks' Lambda, Pillai's trace, Hotelling-Lawley trace, and Roy's root.
Unit 5: Principal Component Analysis (PCA): algebraic derivation, eigenvalue scree plots, and data reduction.

courses.title: Seminar
courses.description: Individual undergraduate academic research seminar. Literature synthesis on a cutting-edge statistical theory or application, written seminar report compilation, and oral presentation before the departmental seminar panel.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Scientific research methodology, topic formulation, and scholarly literature search.
Unit 2: Critical appraisal of published peer-reviewed statistical literature.
Unit 3: Scientific paper structuring, LaTeX / Markdown typesetting, and academic citation standards.
Unit 4: Slide design, scientific storytelling, and visual data representation.
Unit 5: Oral seminar delivery, defense of methodology, and question-and-answer engagement.

courses.title: Operations Research II
courses.description: Advanced operations research techniques: Integer Programming (Branch and Bound, Cutting Plane), Dynamic Programming, Game Theory (two-person zero-sum, saddle points), Queuing Theory (M/M/1, M/M/c), and Project Network Scheduling (CPM/PERT).
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Integer Linear Programming: Gomory's cutting plane algorithm and Branch-and-Bound methods.
Unit 2: Dynamic programming: Bellman's principle of optimality, recursive equations, and stage decisions.
Unit 3: Theory of games: minimax theorem, mixed strategies, linear programming formulation of games.
Unit 4: Queuing models: Poisson arrivals, exponential service times, M/M/1 and M/M/k queuing equations.
Unit 5: Project scheduling: network diagrams, critical path method (CPM), and PERT probabilistic analysis.

courses.title: Statistical Quality Control I
courses.description: Advanced quality engineering: Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) control charts, Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) charts, multivariate quality control charts (Hotelling's T^2 charts), continuous sampling plans, and Six Sigma DMAIC methodologies.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Advanced memory-type control charts: tabular and V-mask Cumulative Sum (CUSUM) charts.
Unit 2: Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) control charts for detecting small process shifts.
Unit 3: Multivariate quality control: Hotelling's T-squared control chart for correlated quality characteristics.
Unit 4: Continuous sampling inspection plans (CSP-1, CSP-2) and sequential sampling plans.
Unit 5: Six Sigma quality framework: DMAIC cycle, gauge repeatability & reproducibility (R&R) studies.

courses.title: Distribution Theory II
courses.description: Multivariate continuous distributions: Multivariate Normal, Wishart distribution, Hotelling's T^2 distribution, distribution of quadratic forms, non-central Chi-square, non-central t and F, and asymptotic distribution theorems.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Matrix-variate distributions and properties of the Wishart distribution.
Unit 2: Derivation and properties of Hotelling's T-squared distribution.
Unit 3: Non-central probability distributions: non-central Chi-Square, non-central t, and non-central F.
Unit 4: Distributions of linear and quadratic forms under multivariate normality.
Unit 5: Asymptotic expansion of distributions, delta method, and saddle-point approximations.

courses.title: Logical Background of Statistics and Decision Theory
courses.description: Philosophical and logical foundations of statistical inference, inductive logic, subjective vs objective probability, Bayesian decision theory, prior and posterior distributions, loss functions, risk functions, minimax and Bayes rules.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Inductive logic, philosophical debates on probability (classical, frequentist, subjective/Bayesian).
Unit 2: Statistical decision problem components: states of nature, actions, loss functions, and risk.
Unit 3: Utility theory axioms, von Neumann-Morgenstern utility, and decision criteria under uncertainty.
Unit 4: Bayesian decision principles: conjugate priors, posterior risk, and optimal Bayes decision rules.
Unit 5: Minimax decision criterion, admissible decision rules, and randomized decision procedures.

courses.title: Stochastic Processes
courses.description: Markov chains in discrete and continuous time, transition probability matrices, Chapman-Kolmogorov equations, classification of states, stationary distributions, Poisson processes, birth-and-death processes, and queuing applications.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Definition of stochastic processes, index sets, state spaces, and Markov property.
Unit 2: Discrete-time Markov Chains: transition probability matrix and Chapman-Kolmogorov equations.
Unit 3: Classification of states: periodicity, recurrence, transience, absorbing states, and ergodicity.
Unit 4: Stationary distributions and long-run limiting behavior of irreducible recurrent chains.
Unit 5: Continuous-time Markov processes: Poisson process, pure birth, and birth-and-death processes.

courses.title: Non–parametric Methods
courses.description: Distribution-free statistical methods: order statistics, Sign test, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, Mann-Whitney U test, Kruskal-Wallis one-way ANOVA by ranks, Friedman two-way ANOVA, Kendall's tau, Spearman's rank correlation, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness-of-fit.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Concepts of non-parametric vs parametric inference, empirical distribution function.
Unit 2: One-sample tests: Sign test, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, and Kolmogorov-Smirnov one-sample test.
Unit 3: Two independent sample tests: Mann-Whitney U test and Kolmogorov-Smirnov two-sample test.
Unit 4: K-sample tests: Kruskal-Wallis test for independent samples and Friedman test for paired data.
Unit 5: Measures of association: Spearman's rank correlation (rho) and Kendall's rank correlation (tau).

courses.title: Multivariate Analysis II
courses.description: Advanced multivariate data analysis: Factor Analysis (orthogonal and oblique rotations), Canonical Correlation Analysis, Linear and Quadratic Discriminant Analysis, Cluster Analysis (hierarchical and k-means), and Multidimensional Scaling.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Exploratory and confirmatory Factor Analysis: principal factor method, varimax rotation, factor scores.
Unit 2: Canonical Correlation Analysis: canonical variates, canonical correlations, and significance tests.
Unit 3: Discriminant Analysis: Fisher's linear discriminant function, classification rules, and error rates.
Unit 4: Cluster Analysis: distance metrics, hierarchical clustering (Ward, complete, average), and K-means.
Unit 5: Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) and Correspondence Analysis for categorical dimensionality reduction.

courses.title: Analysis of Variance II
courses.description: Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA), nested and hierarchical designs, unbalanced ANOVA, mixed and random effects linear models, variance components estimation (ANOVA method, REML), and repeated measures ANOVA.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA): single covariate linear model, test of parallel slopes, adjusted means.
Unit 2: Nested (hierarchical) classification designs: two-stage nested model and ANOVA table.
Unit 3: Unbalanced two-way ANOVA: exact method of fitting constants and weighted squares of means.
Unit 4: Random effects and mixed models: expected mean squares (EMS) and variance components estimation via REML.
Unit 5: Repeated measures ANOVA: sphericity assumption, Mauchly's test, and Greenhouse-Geisser correction.

courses.title: Project
courses.description: Supervised individual final year research project. Independent empirical data collection, statistical modeling, simulation or theoretical contribution, written dissertation submission, and oral defense before external and internal boards.
courses.outline:
Unit 1: Topic selection, hypothesis formulation, research proposal, and supervisor assignment.
Unit 2: Comprehensive literature review and conceptual statistical framework definition.
Unit 3: Methodology formulation, sampling design, data acquisition, and quality validation.
Unit 4: Advanced statistical computation, modeling, hypothesis testing, and empirical interpretations.
Unit 5: Final bound dissertation submission and oral viva voce defense before the examination panel.

staff.bio: Dr. Samuel Ugochukwu Enogwe is a distinguished academic and researcher with extensive expertise in Statistics, Operations Research, and Economics. He began his academic journey at the Federal Polytechnic Nekede, Owerri, Nigeria, earning a Higher National Diploma (HND) in Statistics with Distinction in November 2011. He proceeded to Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike, where he obtained a B.Sc. in Statistics with First Class Honours in November 2015, followed by an M.Sc. in Operations Research in August 2018, graduating as the Overall Best M.Sc. student with a perfect C.G.P.A. of 5.00/5.00. He subsequently earned a Ph.D. in Statistics (Operations Research) from Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, in January 2023, receiving recognition as the Best Graduating Ph.D. student of the Department of Statistics for the 2022/2023 session. Complementing his postgraduate studies, he obtained a Postgraduate Diploma (PGD) in Economics with Distinction from Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike, in January 2026 and is currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Development Economics at the same institution. Dr. Enogwe’s research interests span Statistics, Operations Research, and Economics. His work focuses on developing Batch Arrival Non-Markovian queueing models, designing new statistical distributions for real-world applications, and exploring econometric modeling in development economics. He is highly proficient in statistical and computational tools, including R, Python, and other software packages essential for data-driven research. He has deployed innovative teaching and learning methods to make Statistics accessible and engaging for students and has served as an internal examiner for both Masters’ degree and Ph.D. students. He began his lecturing career at the Department of Mathematics/Statistics, Federal Polytechnic Nekede, Owerri, where he contributed significantly to teaching, research, and community development. He joined Michael Okpara University of Agriculture, Umudike, in 2019 and has been instrumental in the growth and development of the Department of Statistics and the University at large. He has been teaching statistical computing courses in the Department, helping students to utilize various statistical software for data analysis. He has also served as a resource person for MOUAU-LISA, IMSU-LISA, NAU-LISA, and Federal Polytechnic Oko, providing training on R and Python for Data Science. Dr. Enogwe has made significant contributions to university governance and academic service. He serves as the Secretary of the Departmental Academic Quality Assurance Committee (2024–present), member of the Departmental Postgraduate Board (2023–present), and Level Adviser (2021–present). Additionally, he is a member of Examination Moderation Committee (2021-present), Curriculum Review and Development Committee (2021-present), and Documentation & Library Committee for Accreditation (2021-present), Statistics Course Recovery & Harmonization Committee (2025–present), Chairman of the Secretarial sub-committee for the COLPAS Maiden Conference (2025–present), and College Representative to the School of General Studies (2025–present), MOUAU. He currently serves as Publicity Secretary of the Institute of Operational Research and Management Science of Nigeria (IORMS) and previously held the position of Assistant General Secretary (2023–2025). He has served as member Local Organizing Committee (LOC) of Several Conferences. Dr. Enogwe is an active researcher with over 31 peer-reviewed journal publications and 33 conference papers. He is a member of several professional organizations, including the Chartered Institute of Statisticians of Nigeria (CISON), the Professional Statisticians of Nigeria (PSSN), and the International Biometric Society (IBS). He is happily married to Mrs. Chinenye Eucharia Samuel-Enogwe, an English Language expert, and they enjoy a strong and flourishing family life grounded in faith and mutual support.

news.title: UNIZIK Senate Approves First Semester 2026/2027 Academic Calendar: Key Resumption, Matriculation & Exam Dates
news.summary: The Senate of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, at its 246th meeting on September 30, 2026, officially approved the 2026/2027 Academic Calendar (Ref: NAU/R/E/032/97) for regular undergraduate students.
news.content:
The Senate of Nnamdi Azikiwe University, at its 246th meeting held on Wednesday, 30th September 2026, formally approved the Academic Calendar of Events for the 2026/2027 Academic Session for all regular undergraduate students.

In an internal memorandum released by the Office of the Registrar (Ref. No.: NAU/R/E/032/97, dated 2nd October 2026), the university outlined key milestones for the First Semester as follows:

• Resumption & Registration (New Students): Monday, October 12, 2026
• Resumption, Tuition Payment & Course Registration (Returning Students): Wednesday, October 14, 2026
• Convocation Ceremonies (2024/2025 & 2025/2026): Sunday, November 15 – Friday, November 20, 2026
• University-Wide Quiz: Monday, November 30, 2026
• Vacation, Christmas & Election Break: Wednesday, December 23, 2026 – Saturday, January 22, 2027
• All Students Return to Campus: Saturday, January 23, 2027
• First Semester Lectures Resume: Monday, January 25, 2027
• Matriculation Ceremony: Friday, January 29, 2027
• Revision Week: Monday, February 15, 2027
• First Semester Degree Examinations (CBE & PBE): Monday, February 22 – Friday, March 19, 2027
• School of General Studies (GS) Examinations: Monday, March 15 – Friday, March 19, 2027
• End of First Semester Examinations: Friday, March 19, 2027
• Vacation and Easter Break: Saturday, March 20 – Friday, April 2, 2027

All students of the Department of Statistics are instructed to observe these dates strictly.

news.content:
In compliance with university directives from the Registrar, the Department of Statistics announces resumption protocols for all undergraduate cohorts:

1. New Students (100 Level & Direct Entry):
Resumption is slated for Monday, October 12, 2026. Newly admitted candidates are expected to conclude physical verification, biometrics, student file documentation, and attend inaugural departmental orientation sessions.

2. Old Students (200L, 300L & 400L):
Returning undergraduates return to campus on Wednesday, October 14, 2026. Payment of university school charges, departmental association dues, and online course registration on the UNIZIK portal will commence immediately.

Course registration slips must be presented to Level Course Advisers for physical endorsement within the first two weeks of resumption.

faqs.question: What are the minimum credit units required to graduate from Statistics at UNIZIK?
faqs.answer: Undergraduate students must register and pass all departmental and faculty required core courses across levels 100 to 400, accumulating a minimum of 130 to 144 credit units depending on direct entry or UTME matriculation mode.

faqs.question: When is the SIWES industrial training scheduled and how long does it last?
faqs.answer: SIWES takes place at the 300 Level during the second semester break and lasts for a mandatory period of six (6) months. Students submit weekly logbooks, undergo institutional supervision, and defend their technical report.

faqs.question: What statistical software packages are accepted for final-year project analysis?
faqs.answer: The Department of Statistics standardly approves R (RStudio), Python (Pandas/Statsmodels/Scikit-Learn), SPSS, and SAS. Code scripts, reproducibility files, and raw data matrices must be submitted alongside the thesis.

faqs.question: How can I get departmental course registration forms signed by the Academic Adviser?
faqs.answer: Download your generated course registration slip from the UNIZIK portal, print three (3) copies, and visit your level course adviser during official consultation hours (Mondays and Wednesdays, 10:00 AM - 1:00 PM).

faqs.question: Where is the NASS Secretariat located on campus?
faqs.answer: The NASS Secretariat is located on the Ground Floor of the Faculty of Physical Sciences / Department of Statistics Building, UNIZIK Awka Main Campus.

faqs.question: How do I access past examination questions and course lecture notes?
faqs.answer: Students can download archived past questions and syllabi directly from the Academic Resources & Timetable section on this portal or visit the NASS Departmental Library.
